**Description**
Build the software platform that powers a global operations program. We are a tech team embedded directly in a program organization, building and operating the systems that give program leaders full visibility while giving the operating teams that execute the work secure, scoped access to only their own data.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
As a Software Development Engineer On This Team, You Will Own Services End To End. You Will Design And Ship Multi-tenant Web Applications And APIs That
  
  

* Centralize program operations: campaign rollout, workflow distribution, policy updates, and compliance tasks delivered to the right teams at the right time.
* Enforce strict data boundaries: each operating team sees only its own data; the central program team sees the full picture.
* Integrate modern enterprise authentication across multiple identity environments.
* Operate at scale and in production, with ownership for design, deployment, security review, on-call response, and continuous improvement.
* You will build on AWS using CDK, deploy through staged pipelines, navigate security review processes, and work with security, operations, and business partners across time zones. This is a role where your software directly shapes how a global operations program runs.

A day in the life
  
  
On a typical day, you'll spend most of your time building the software that keeps a global operations program running. That might mean designing a new feature with another engineer in the morning, writing CDK and TypeScript to ship it, pairing on a tricky multi-tenant data problem, or reviewing a teammate's code. You'll run your own services, which means you'll be on call in rotation and will own the incidents and improvements that come with that.
  
  
A lot of your work happens with people, not just with code. You'll partner with security engineers on reviews before a feature launches, work with operations teams on how a new workflow should actually behave in production, and sit down with program leaders to understand what the platform needs to do next.
  
  
**About The Team**
We're a small team that wears many hats. Most of us have a primary specialty: software development, network engineering, security consultation, or governance. We all collaborate across those lines every day. Our mission is to build and run the software platform that powers a global operations program. Our customers are the program leaders who shape the strategy, the operating teams who execute it, and the security reviewers and business owners we work with. We care about shipping, learning from each other, and solving the problem in front of us. Come help us figure it out.

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience

* Experience programming with at least one software programming language
* Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems
* Working knowledge of using large language model (LLM) tools (such as Claude, Kiro, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot) to generate code and shape architecture decisions. Foundational experience is sufficient; openness to learning new models and tools is expected.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Experience architecting/operating solutions built on AWS
* Experience managing data pipelines
* Experience in application security architecture, security code reviews, security testing, incident response, or security infrastructure
* Experience managing full application stacks from the OS up through custom applications, or experience in web security and experience in deploying identity and access management systems
* Experience working cross-functionally and driving decision making among stakeholders with competing goals

**About The Role**
What if the code you write could directly shape how the next generation of AI understands and generates software? We're looking for Software Engineers in Portland to build, evaluate, and improve AI-generated code — helping train AI systems to think like real developers.
  
  
You'll write solutions, review AI outputs, and provide the expert-level feedback that makes AI coding assistants smarter, safer, and more reliable. This is hands-on engineering work at the frontier of AI development — not theoretical, not bureaucratic, and not boring.
  
  
This is a fully remote, flexible contract role. If you can write clean code and explain your reasoning, we want to hear from you.
  
  

* Organization: Alignerr
* Type: Hourly Contract
* Location: Remote
* Commitment: 10–40 hours/week

**What You'll Do**

* Write, debug, and optimize code across a range of languages, frameworks, and problem domains
* Review and evaluate AI-generated code for correctness, efficiency, readability, and best practices
* Identify bugs, logic errors, security issues, and performance bottlenecks in AI outputs
* Provide structured, detailed feedback explaining why code works — or doesn't
* Design challenging coding prompts and edge-case scenarios to stress-test AI capabilities
* Compare and rank multiple AI-generated solutions based on engineering quality
* Work independently and asynchronously — fully on your own schedule

**Who You Are**

* Proficient in one or more programming languages (Python, JavaScript, Java, C++, Go, TypeScript, or similar)
* Solid understanding of data structures, algorithms, and software design principles
* Able to read, write, and reason about code with clarity and precision
* Strong problem-solving instincts and a systematic debugging approach
* Clear written communicator — you can explain technical decisions in plain language
* Self-motivated and reliable when working independently without supervision
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience

**Nice to Have**

* Experience across multiple languages or tech stacks (full-stack, backend, systems, data engineering)
* Familiarity with AI/ML concepts, LLMs, or prompt engineering
* Background in code review, technical writing, or mentoring junior developers
* Experience with cloud platforms, DevOps, or distributed systems
* Competitive programming, open-source contributions, or side projects that demonstrate your craft
* Advanced degree in Computer Science or related discipline

**Why Join Us**

* Work on cutting-edge AI projects alongside leading research labs
* Fully remote and flexible — set your own hours and work from anywhere
* Freelance autonomy with intellectually stimulating, high-impact work
* Directly influence how AI writes, understands, and reasons about code
* Sharpen your own engineering skills by evaluating diverse problems daily
* Potential for ongoing work and contract extension as new projects launch

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.
  
  
Join us to put AI to work for people.
  
  
**Job Description**
**Team bio**
ServiceNow’s Applied AI Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) team is where bold ideas meet real-world impact. We work with our most strategic customers to shape the future of enterprise AI. We find high-value opportunities, speed up business outcomes, and build reusable AI-native solutions that make the ServiceNow AI Platform even better.
  
  
**Why this internship matters**
Enterprises want AI that delivers real value, not just potential. Our Associate FDEs turn the latest LLM capabilities into secure, scalable software that customers rely on. As an Associate FDE Intern, you’ll learn how that happens by doing it. You’ll join a live delivery team, build real features, and see how great engineers take an idea from whiteboard to working solution.
  
  
**Who You Are**
You’re a curious, hands-on builder who likes making things work. You’ve experimented with LLMs, APIs, or AI tools in class projects, hackathons, or on your own time. You enjoy solving messy problems, you ask good questions, and you want to understand why something matters to the people using it, not just how it works.
  
  
**Location: Expectations to be hybrid in office - either Santa Clara, CA or New York, NY**
**What You’ll Do**

* Build and test components of LLM-enabled applications, including backend services, data pipelines, prompts, and UI elements, under the guidance of senior FDSEs
* Join customer working sessions to see how FDEs uncover problems, scope solutions, and iterate quickly
* Help create reusable assets such as code samples, prompt libraries, scaffolds, and documentation that speed up future projects
* Prototype and evaluate new AI techniques (retrieval, agents, prompt chaining) and share what you learn with the team
* Work in agile sprints, with code reviews, stand-ups, and demos
* Deliver an internship project and present it to FDE and product leaders at the end of your program

**What Success Looks Like**

* Shipped contribution: Your code or assets are used in a real customer build or internal tool
* Reusable impact: You leave behind at least one documented pattern, prompt set, or scaffold the team keeps using
* Growth: You get noticeably stronger at full-stack engineering, LLM tooling, and working with customers
* Clear communication: You can explain what you built, why it matters, and what you’d do next

**Qualifications**
**What you bring**

* AI curiosity: Experience using or thinking critically about how AI can improve work, decisions, or problem-solving, whether through coursework, projects, hackathons, or personal experiments

- Education: Currently enrolled full-time in an accredited university pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field.

* Expected Bachelors graduation date of May 2028 or later, with plans to return to studies following the internship.
* Available to work full-time for 12 weeks during the summer.
* Programming fundamentals: Comfort with at least one language such as Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Java
* Web basics: Familiarity with REST APIs and a frontend framework such as React or Angular
* LLM exposure: Hands-on experience with an LLM API or framework (for example, LangChain or Semantic Kernel), prompt design, or vector search
* Problem-solving mindset: Able to break down unclear problems, try things quickly, and learn from what doesn’t work
* Collaboration: Clear communicator who enjoys working with teammates and is comfortable asking for help
* Eligibility: Authorized to work in USA for the duration of the internship [confirm with Talent Acquisition]

**Nice to have**

* Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), Git, containers, or CI/CD
* Familiarity with SQL, pandas, or basic ML concepts
* A portfolio, GitHub profile, or project demo you’re proud of
* Interest in enterprise SaaS platforms such as ServiceNow

**Responsibilities**
The E-commerce Recommendation Foundation team is dedicated to building the next-generation recommendation intelligence. We aim to develop a unified Foundation Model that supports multi-business and multi-scenario recommendation systems, covering the full pipeline from retrieval and ranking to re-ranking, and driving a comprehensive upgrade in intelligence and generative capability.
  
  
We believe the future of recommendation systems goes beyond predicting click-through rates — it lies in understanding the relationship between people and content, and in generating new connections. The team is exploring an event-sequence-driven generative recommendation paradigm, deeply integrating large language models (LLMs), multimodal understanding, reinforcement learning, and system optimization to advance recommendation systems toward general-purpose intelligent agents.
  
  
We value original exploration and encourage both research thinking and engineering excellence. Every team member is empowered to propose hypotheses and validate ideas in an open environment — your code and papers may help define the next paradigm of recommendation systems. We seek individuals with a general intelligence mindset to join us in redefining the future of recommendation.
  
  
Responsibilities:
  
- Build and optimize cross-scenario shared Foundation Models to enable unified modeling and efficient inference. Advance the event-sequence-driven generative recommendation paradigm, integrating multimodal understanding and generative capabilities.
  
- Apply LLM technologies across retrieval, ranking, and re-ranking stages; participate in model training, inference optimization, and system co-design.
  
- Explore the integration of LLMs / VLMs with recommendation systems to develop adaptive and evolving intelligent recommenders.
  
- Research end-to-end generative recommendation and system optimization methods that balance efficiency and user experience.
  
  
**Qualifications**
Minimum Qualifications
  
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field.
  
- 1+ years of experience in machine learning, deep learning, or information retrieval.
  
- Proficiency in Python and familiarity with mainstream deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch).
  
- Strong passion for intelligent recommendation systems and a self-driven research mindset.
  
  
Preferred Qualifications
  
- PhD degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field.
  
- Experience in large-scale recommendation system development or large-model training, with notable technical achievements in a sub-area.
  
- Research experience or publications in LLMs, multimodal learning, reinforcement learning, or generative recommendation.
  
- Familiarity with pre-training and post-training processes for large language models (LLMs) or Foundation Models.

**Responsibilities**
The Product Data Analytics Team analyzes a combination of product usage and product performance data to derive meaningful insights that would serve as a guide to better product and decision making for our business leaders.
  
As a member of the data science team, you will work with diverse and highly collaborative teams of product managers, engineers, and other data analysts to drive product impact. You will be working on exciting and challenging projects, and convert the insights into real changes, for both new initiatives and scaled products. You are a self-starter who is excited about data, excels in product logic thinking, clear communication, and brings distinctive problem-solving skills and impeccable quantitative modeling experience.
  
  
As a Data Scientist, you will be working on designing and monitoring core metrics, identifying the root causes for metric movements through deep dive into the models. The role will cover a wide range of model-driven solutions to deliver superior business outcomes through research and analyses. In particular, this role will leverage the causal structure of user behavior, identify trends and opportunities for user growth and great ecosystem, and guide the product team to make best decisions.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
- Leverage data to solve challenging business problems from full-spectrum of product and business lines, using analytical and statistical approaches.
  
- Build and improve applicable statistical models, e.g. LTV and ROI prediction, to guide user growth-related decisions.
  
- Initiate model-driven analysis to provide deep insights into various products. Catch the common rule of problems and establish the inter-product analytic paradigm.
  
- Work with Product, Operations, Engineering and cross-functional teams to drive product development through analytic, statistical, and algorithmic expertise
  
- Design, run and analyze A/B experiments to inform and execute the product strategy, and ultimately improve the product and support business decisions.

- Bachelor's degree in a quantitative discipline (e.g. Statistics, Operations Research, Computational Biology, Computer Science, Mathematics, Economics).
  
- 2+ years of experience in statistical modeling (Regression, Classification, Clustering, etc.) and machine learning (deep learning), and experience in user-level modeling
  
- Ability to conduct rigorous analysis and communicate conclusions to both technical and non-technical audiences
  
- Proficiency in SQL, Python/R

- Solid communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively with internal teams in a diversified environment
  
- Passion for the Internet industry and data analysis.
  
- Self-starter with the ability to acquire an in-depth understanding of the relation between data and user experience/product growth.

Blue Orange Digital is a data engineering and AI consultancy that builds production-grade data platforms, ML systems, and GenAI solutions for companies that take their data seriously. We are not a staff augmentation shop or a slide-deck consultancy. We are builders. Our teams embed directly into client organizations, shipping code alongside their teams to accelerate delivery and build lasting capability.
  
  
Our clients include Fortune 500 enterprises and high-growth startups across industries. We partner with Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, GCP, and Azure to deliver battle-tested solutions that drive measurable ROI.

Independent Contractor (with potential transition to full‑time employment)
  
  
****Position overview:****
This is the person we send into a client when the problem is not yet a spec. You sit with their operators, finance leads, and analysts, watch how work actually gets done, and turn messy real-world processes into agentic AI workflows that hold up in production.
  
  
You are dual-fluent by design. In the morning you map a claims-handling or order-to-cash process with a business owner who has never written a line of code. In the afternoon you wire that process into an agent that calls their CRM, queries their warehouse, and routes exceptions to the right human. You translate in both directions, turning vague business pain into concrete technical scope, and turning technical constraints into options a non-technical stakeholder can decide on.
  
  
The role is a balanced bridge. Roughly half your time is discovery, facilitation, and trust-building with client teams. The other half is hands-on engineering: building the agent logic, the integrations, and the evaluation that proves it works. You will not stop at a prototype. You ship the workflow, instrument it, and hand over something the client can run and extend.
  
  
****Responsibilities:****

* Embed with client teams to understand how work actually happens, shadowing operators and mapping processes that live in people's heads, spreadsheets, and a dozen disconnected tools
* Break down complex business processes into agentic workflows: decompose a goal into steps, decide what an agent automates versus where a human stays in the loop, and design the tool-use and decision logic to match
* Build production-grade agentic workflows using frameworks like LangGraph and LangChain, including tool calling, memory, routing, retries, and clean failure recovery
* Build integrations to the data and operational systems that workflows depend on: CRMs, ERPs, ticketing systems, data warehouses, internal APIs, and document stores, handling auth, rate limits, and reliability
* Enable core platform capabilities that the whole engagement reuses: retrieval over client documents, structured output and function calling, prompt versioning, logging, and observability
* Design evaluation and guardrails that make a workflow trustworthy in an enterprise setting: task-specific evals, regression checks, PII handling, and human review steps where the stakes demand them
* Run working sessions and demos that keep business stakeholders bought in, translating technical tradeoffs into clear decisions about cost, risk, and timeline
* Document what you build and hand it over cleanly, so client teams can operate and extend the workflows after the engagement
* Bring patterns back to BOD, turning what worked on one engagement into reusable building blocks for the next

****Requirements:****

* 3 or more years of software engineering experience building systems that run in production, plus the judgment to know what production-ready means
* Hands-on experience building with LLMs: prompting, function calling, structured output, retrieval, and at least one agent or multi-step workflow you took past the prototype stage
* Strong integration skills, you have connected real systems through REST APIs, webhooks, SDKs, and databases, and dealt with auth, pagination, rate limits, and flaky upstreams
* Proficiency in Python, comfort with async patterns, API design, and the data-pipeline reliability that agentic workflows live or die on
* Working knowledge of SQL and data systems, enough to pull what a workflow needs from a client's warehouse or operational database
* Real client-facing or cross-functional skill: you can sit with a non-technical stakeholder, draw out how their process works, and earn their trust without talking down to them
* Strong written and verbal communication, you can explain why an agent took a wrong turn, or why a manual step should stay manual, to a business owner without losing them
* A bias toward shipping, you would rather get a working workflow in front of users this week than perfect an architecture diagram
* Production experience with agent frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) or building custom orchestration
* Experience with RAG systems: chunking, embeddings, vector stores (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, pgvector), and re-ranking

****Preferred qualifications:****

* Familiarity with LLM evaluation: task-specific metrics, LLM-as-judge, and regression test suites
* Background in process mapping, solutions engineering, forward-deployed work, or technical consulting across concurrent engagements
* Experience with workflow and integration platforms (Temporal, Airflow, Zapier, n8n) or iPaaS tooling
* Exposure to a major cloud and its AI services (AWS Bedrock or SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, Azure ML)

* Problems that matter, real client processes with real constraints, not greenfield sandboxes

* Direct access to modern AI infrastructure: AWS, GCP, Azure, Databricks, Snowflake, and the open-source ecosystem

* Professional development budget and certification support
* A team that will push back on your design decisions and make them better
* Unlimited Paid Time Off (PTO)

Craftbridge Digital builds web apps, API integrations and automation scripts for businesses, and keeps their older software running. We're based in Austin.
  
  
We're hiring a Software Engineer. Full-time, remote from anywhere in the United States.
  
  
A typical ticket: a client's order form has to push data into their accounting system, and nobody wrote down how the old sync worked.
  
  
You read the code that's there, write the new piece, test it against a copy of their data and ship it with a short note on what changed.

At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.

  

This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.

  

Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!

**The Team**

  

The Automated Driving Advanced Development division bridges TRI research and Toyota products. In partnership with Woven by Toyota, the team is researching and developing an end-to-end learned driving stack that maps sensor inputs directly to planned trajectories.

  

**The Internship**

  

We’re seeking a research intern to investigate how driving policies post-trained in fast, low-fidelity simulation can transfer to higher-fidelity simulation and real-world driving. This is an open research problem: differences in sensor inputs, vehicle dynamics, and other agents can limit transfer, and policies may learn simulator-specific behavior or forget previously learned skills.

  

You’ll lead an independent research project exploring approaches to sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer for sensor-based driving models. You’ll work with Toyota driving data, generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure, with the goal of producing work suitable for a conference or workshop submission.

  

**The Opportunity**

  

As a research intern on AD2, you will own a standalone research project in sim-to-sim and sim-to-real domain mapping, with the opportunity to:

  

  
* Drive your own research: Shape the approach, run experiments, and analyze results, with the independence to set your own direction.
  
* Publish your findings: The project is designed to produce results suitable for a conference or workshop publication.
  
* Shape a real autonomy model: The tools and insights you create will help the team post-train our autonomy model more effectively, with the potential to influence the autonomy stack eventually deployed in Toyota vehicles.
  
* Collaborate with experienced researchers: Work closely with a small team of industry-leading researchers with deep experience in robotics and autonomous driving.
  
* Work at scale: Use the same large-scale Toyota driving data, base models, and simulation infrastructure the team uses every day.
  
  

  

You can learn more about our work on the Automated Driving Advanced Development team page.

**Responsibilities**
  

  
* Conduct research to advance the state of the art in sim-to-sim and sim-to-real domain mapping, enabling driving policies post-trained in fast, low-fidelity simulation to transfer to higher-fidelity simulation and real-world driving
  
* Design and run experiments using large-scale Toyota driving data, the team’s generative base models, and closed-loop simulation infrastructure
  
* Perform closed-loop evaluations across simulators of varying fidelity, and develop metrics that measure how well post-trained behaviors carry over between domains
  
* Collaborate with researchers and engineers to integrate the tools and findings from your project into the team’s model development and post-training workflows
  
* Present progress and results regularly to the team, and incorporate feedback into the research direction
  
* Write up your findings as a paper for submission to a conference or workshop by the end of the internship
  
  

  
**Qualifications**
  

  
* Currently pursuing a Ph.D. or master’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Engineering, or a related field
  
* Proficiency in Python and ML frameworks such as PyTorch for implementing and evaluating research ideas, along with an understanding of version control, testing, and software engineering fundamentals
  
* Research experience in one or more of the following: sim-to-real transfer, domain adaptation, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, generative models such as diffusion or flow matching, or autonomous driving
  
* Demonstrated research ability, such as publications, preprints, or substantial independent research projects
  
* Ability to work independently on an open-ended research problem, and to communicate methods and results clearly
  
* Able to work in a hybrid in-office arrangement at TRI’s headquarters in Los Altos, California, for the full 12-week internship
  
  

  
**Bonus Qualifications**
  

  
* Experience with driving or robotics simulators such as CARLA or NVIDIA DriveSim, or with sensor simulation and neural rendering
  
* Experience with world models or generative models for video or scene reconstruction
  
* Experience post-training policies with reinforcement learning, DAgger, or preference-based methods
  
* Hands-on experience working with real-world sensor data, such as video, lidar, IMU, or radar
  
* Experience with large-scale distributed training and experiment tracking tools such as Weights & Biases
  
* Publications at venues such as CoRL, ICRA, RSS, NeurIPS, ICML, or CVPR

**About The Role**
Fleet Farm is looking for a motivated, technically skilled Asset Protection Data Analyst to help transform how we use data to reduce loss, identify risk, and improve profitability. This newly created role will focus on developing meaningful business intelligence, improving reporting capabilities, and turning complex information into practical recommendations for store and district leadership.
  
  
Reporting directly to the Vice President of Asset Protection, you'll have the opportunity to take ownership of key analytical tools, introduce innovative solutions, and help build a more proactive, data-driven Asset Protection function. Previous Asset Protection experience is not required. We're looking for someone who brings strong analytical capabilities, curiosity, and a passion for solving problems.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Analyze transactional, inventory, financial, and operational data to identify shrink trends, fraud indicators, process inefficiencies, and opportunities to improve profitability.
* Become the primary subject matter expert for our Appriss exception-based reporting platform, identifying high-risk transactions and maximizing its reporting capabilities.
* Develop and enhance dashboards, automated reports, and analytical tools using Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar technologies to deliver accurate, actionable insights.
* Create store-specific reporting that identifies trends, prioritizes opportunities, and provides clear recommendations to Asset Protection district managers and store leadership.
* Connect data across multiple systems to uncover patterns, identify root causes, and distinguish store-level challenges from broader operational or process issues.
* Collaborate with Asset Protection, Inventory Control, Store Operations, and IT to improve data accuracy, streamline investigative referrals, and establish consistent reporting processes.
* Explore emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, and automation to improve analytical efficiency, reduce manual processes, and continuously enhance reporting capabilities.

Job Requirements
  
  

* Associate's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience required; bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Business, Finance, Information Systems, or a related field preferred.
* 2+ years of experience in data analytics, business intelligence, financial analysis, inventory analytics, or a related analytical field; retail or Asset Protection experience is a plus, but not required.
* Strong proficiency in Excel and SQL, with experience extracting, manipulating, and interpreting complex data; knowledge of pivot tables, lookups, and Power Query preferred.
* Experience creating dashboards, reports, or data visualizations using Power BI, Tableau, or similar business intelligence tools; exposure to reporting automation or AI-powered analytical tools is a plus.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills with the ability to work independently, learn new technologies, collaborate across departments, and translate complex findings into actionable business recommendations.

Why Fleet Farm?

The Treasury Liquidity Data Analyst reports to the Liquidity Manager and helps modernize the team's data, analytics, and operating capabilities. Working within the bank's first-line liquidity risk function, the analyst uses SQL, Python, automation, and applied artificial intelligence to improve how liquidity data is sourced, validated, analyzed, measured, and communicated. The role identifies manual or inefficient processes, develops scalable solutions, and strengthens recurring analytics and reporting through well-controlled automation. The analyst also builds and supports AI-enabled tools and agents that accelerate research, exception identification, documentation, and management reporting, while maintaining appropriate human review, data governance, information security, and change-control standards. Liquidity risk provides the business foundation for the role, and the successful candidate will develop an understanding of liquidity monitoring, cash flow forecasting, contingency funding, and balance-sheet behavior. The ideal candidate brings strong technical curiosity and a continuous-improvement mindset.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

* Use SQL and Python to source, combine, transform, validate, and analyze balance-sheet, deposit, funding, cash flow, and liquidity data from multiple systems.
* Automate recurring workflows, reconciliations, controls, analysis, and management reporting to reduce manual effort, improve scalability, and ensure timely, repeatable execution.
* Assess existing processes and data flows, identify root causes of inefficiency and data-quality issues, and implement practical, well-documented improvements with measurable outcomes.
* Design, prototype, test, and maintain AI-enabled tools and agents that support research, data validation, exception identification, workflow orchestration, documentation, and insight generation.
* Apply disciplined governance to data, automation, and AI solutions, including requirements documentation, source-to-output traceability, validation and testing, human review, access controls, change management, and ongoing performance monitoring.
* Develop clear analytical outputs and visualizations that explain trends, exceptions, and key drivers to Treasury leadership and cross-functional partners.
* Apply these capabilities to the team's core liquidity responsibilities, including liquidity monitoring and metrics, long-term cash flow forecasting, Contingency Funding Plan activities, control execution, and regulatory reporting support.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Two or more years of relevant experience in data analytics, automation, financial analysis, Treasury, banking, financial risk, consulting, or financial technology.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Two to four years of relevant professional experience in data analysis, process automation, financial datasets, or risk and Treasury applications.
* Working proficiency with SQL and Python for data analysis and automation, including querying, reconciling, and validating data across datasets; using libraries and tools such as pandas, NumPy, Jupyter, and Git; and developing reusable, well-documented code and data-quality checks.
* Experience building automated data pipelines, reconciliations, exception reports, dashboards, controls, or management information, and working with balance-sheet, deposit, funding, cash flow, general-ledger, or other financial datasets.
* Practical familiarity with generative AI, including experience developing, prototyping, or supporting AI-enabled workflows or agents using Python, APIs, or approved enterprise tools, and exposure to large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt design, or agent frameworks.
* Demonstrated ability to evaluate manual or inefficient processes, translate business needs into technical requirements, and implement controlled, sustainable improvements.
* Exposure to Treasury, liquidity risk, asset-liability management, cash flow forecasting, contingency funding, stress testing, or regulatory reporting.
* Awareness of data governance, responsible AI, model risk, information security, software-development controls, or change-management practices in a regulated environment.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, and familiarity with data visualization or business intelligence tools.

Rezolute is a late-stage rare disease biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative therapies for patients living with severe metabolic and endocrine disorders. Our mission is to bring hope and meaningful solutions to patients and families affected by rare and difficult-to-treat diseases through scientific innovation, collaboration, and integrity.
  
  
Rezolute’s lead investigational therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is a fully human monoclonal antibody in late-stage clinical development for the treatment of hypoglycemia due to congenital and acquired forms of hyperinsulinism (HI). As Rezolute expands its medical and scientific focus into
**tumor-related hyperinsulinism (tumor HI),**
most commonly related to pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (insulinomas) or paraneoplastic hypoglycemia (NICTH), the company is committed to advancing novel therapeutic strategies that address this rare and complex form of hypoglycemia associated with insulin-secreting tumors and related neuro-oncology disorders.
  
  
More information can be found at rezolutebio.com
  
  
**Position Summary**
Rezolute is seeking a Data Analyst II to turn complex data into actionable insights supporting commercial planning, medical affairs, and business decision-making. This hands-on role combines data management, coding, analysis, and visualization to help teams better understand patient populations, healthcare providers, treatment patterns, and market opportunities.
  
  
The Data Analyst II will use AWS, Snowflake, SQL, and Python or R to integrate data, automate analytical workflows, and develop reliable datasets and reporting solutions. Working closely with business stakeholders, this individual will translate questions into structured analyses and communicate findings through clear visualizations, reports, and presentations.
  
  
The ideal candidate brings strong technical skills, sound analytical judgment, and a collaborative, self-directed approach. Experience with healthcare claims or other pharmaceutical industry data is a plus.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Acquire, clean, integrate, and manage healthcare and business data using AWS, Snowflake, SQL, and Python or R.
* Build, deploy, and maintain reusable data pipelines, analytical datasets, and scheduled code in AWS and Snowflake.
* Develop a strong working knowledge of healthcare data and the biopharmaceutical industry, including how claims, provider, and market data reflect patient care and business activity.
* Conduct exploratory and statistical analyses to identify trends, answer business questions, and generate actionable insights.
* Apply statistical and machine learning methods, where appropriate, to support patient identification, segmentation, and prioritization, with clear documentation of methods, validation, and limitations.
* Support analyses of patient populations, healthcare providers and organizations, treatment patterns, market dynamics, and field-team activity.
* Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations in Power BI, Tableau, Python, or comparable tools.
* Automate recurring data preparation, quality checks, and reporting processes to reduce manual effort.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree with a minimum of 3 years' experience in a quantitative or technical field, such as statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, or engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
* Relevant professional experience in data analytics, data management, analytics engineering, or a related field.
* Hands-on experience with AWS and Snowflake for data storage, querying, transformation, or analytical workflows.
* Strong SQL skills and proficiency in Python or R for data manipulation, analysis, and automation.
* Experience cleaning, combining, and analyzing large or complex datasets.
* Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint for analysis and communication.
* Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with others.

**Preferred Attributes**

* Experience with Databricks, Snowflake or Azure in addition to AWS.
* Familiarity with JavaScript frontend frameworks or Python application frameworks.
* Experience supporting cloud migrations, workflow automation, or data platform modernization.
* Experience using company-approved AI-enabled tools for coding, testing, or documentation, with appropriate attention to security and output validation.

**Description**
ARCADE is the Science and Analytics team for Amazon Multi-Channel Fulfillment and Commerce (MCCF). ARCADE owns the science behind MCCF's core business decisions. That includes MCF demand forecasting for US and International markets, which feeds capacity planning and OP commitments. It also includes pricing science, from elasticity studies to custom pricing recommendations for enterprise accounts. For Sales and Account Management, we build the merchant retention and propensity models they use to decide which merchants to focus on. We also design and measure experiments for MCCF programs and build models that support ASCS service quality. Each of these runs as a governed mechanism within the business, not a one-off analysis.
  
  
In 2027 we're investing into forecasting, measurement and automation. On forecasting, we'll make MCF demand forecasts more accurate and extend regional forecasts to International markets. We'll also build a per-merchant baseline of organic growth. That baseline lets teams measure how much account management actions, product features and discounts actually add, and spot declining merchants early. On automation, we'll automate custom pricing recommendations for enterprise accounts through PRISM. Over the 3-year plan, we'll add cost-to-serve modeling, a supply chain optimizer for inbound placement and routing and a shared framework for monitoring all production models.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Build, deploy and maintain ML and statistical models for MCF demand forecasting, merchant growth, retention and propensity, and pricing
* Design and analyze A/B tests and causal studies to measure the impact of account management actions, product features, discounts and pricing changes
* Build the per-merchant organic growth baseline and make it available to Sales, Account Management, Product and Finance for measuring impact and monitoring merchant health
* Automate decisions that are made by hand today, including custom pricing recommendations for enterprise accounts (PRISM) and ASCS service interaction categorization and quality scoring
* Help build the 3-year-plan models: cost-to-serve, supply chain optimization for inbound placement and routing, and ASCS cross-service propensity
* Help build a shared framework for monitoring production models for drift, data quality and accuracy
* Turn unclear business questions into scoped science problems with clear success metrics, working with the eight business teams ARCADE supports
* Work with BIEs and Economics on data, features and metric definitions, using ARCADE's governed datasets
* Feed model outputs into WBR, QBR and OP planning cycles, and write narrative documents with recommendations for senior leaders
* Raise science standards on the team through code and design reviews, reusable tools and documentation

**Basic Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM), or experience working in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
* 2+ years of data scientist experience
* 3+ years of data querying languages (e.g. SQL), scripting languages (e.g. Python) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, Matlab, etc.) experience
* 3+ years of machine learning/statistical modeling data analysis tools and techniques, and parameters that affect their performance experience
* 1+ years of working with or evaluating AI systems experience

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ph.D. in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM)
* Knowledge of machine learning concepts and their application to reasoning and problem-solving
* Experience in defining and creating benchmarks for assessing GenAI model performance
* Experience applying quantitative analysis to solve business problems and making data-driven business decisions
* Experience effectively communicating complex concepts through written and verbal communication

**Description**
Amazon’s third-party marketplace is a multibillion-dollar global ecosystem, connecting customers and sellers across the world through millions of transactions annually. The Seller Fee Science Team integrates economic modeling, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to guide business fee strategy, ensure fees are accurately computed for millions of products, and improves the seller experience with AI tools that support any fee related contact (understanding, audit, and dispute). We build the scientific foundation that empowers sellers to grow their businesses with clarity and confidence.
  
  
Our team brings together world-class economists, physicists, mathematicians, and computer scientists to tackle diverse challenging problems that require theoretical rigor and deliver real-world impact. For example, precision measurement of difficult to measure products, large-scale simulation of sales, inventory, and policy changes, as well as leveraging natural language understanding and automated reasoning to interpret policy, generate code, resolve disputes, audit fees, and respond to sellers at meaninful scale.
  
  
As an applied scientist on our team, this role will focus on the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence to predict and reconcile measurement of products globally. This blends together statistical modeling, application of NLP, image processing, classical machine learning, cost-benefit analysis, causal modeling, and optimization. Your work will shape not only how fees are implemented, but how they are interpreted, experienced, and trusted at scale. You will partner closely with engineers and product partners to take your solutions from research to production.
  
  
We are seeking scientists who are motivated by first principles, disciplined experimentation, and the technical challenge of deploying ideas at global scale. This is an opportunity to work on consequential problems where mathematical rigor meets real-world complexity, and where your models, algorithms, and systems will directly influence the experience of millions of sellers. * Apply rigorous experimentation, causal inference, and simulation methods to validate models and quantify business impact at scale.
* Communicate scientific innovations and results clearly to cross-functional stakeholders and contribute to the broader internal and external scientific community through publications, talks, and technical artifacts.

**Description**
Amazon DynamoDB powers many of the world's fastest-growing businesses, including Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin. It also powers enterprises such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One. Within Amazon, it runs high-traffic properties including Alexa, Amazon.com, and every Amazon fulfillment center. DynamoDB is one of the largest distributed database systems in the world. We believe it is always Day 1, and we keep improving the service and adding new capabilities.
  
  
DynamoDB is a serverless, fully managed database. It delivers consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, with no servers to provision, no maintenance windows, and no downtime. Customers can create a table and scale it automatically to their most demanding workloads without having to plan capacity. During Prime Day 2026, DynamoDB handled more than 59 trillion requests over four days. It peaked at 192 million requests per second while keeping single-digit millisecond response times. The Capacity & Customer Entitlement (CCE) team builds the systems behind this. We decide how much throughput and storage each customer gets and enforce quotas and limits fairly. We also keep DynamoDB's global fleet ahead of demand. When our systems do their job, customers grow without thinking about capacity, and DynamoDB runs efficiently at any scale.
  
  
Managing capacity for one of the largest databases in the world is a hard distributed systems problem. Our systems forecast demand across every AWS Region, plan and place capacity across the fleet, and manage the limits and entitlements that decide how far each customer can scale. We prepare DynamoDB for major events such as Prime Day and new Region launches, so capacity is in place well before customers need it. We are building fully automated capacity management from the ground up. It is a greenfield opportunity to design systems that detect, predict, and act on their own. Engineers on this team solve problems where accuracy, scale, and cost all matter at the same time, and their work shapes how customers experience DynamoDB.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design, build, and operate the services that manage DynamoDB throughput, storage, quotas, and customer entitlements at global scale.
* Build automated capacity management: demand forecasting, proactive scaling, and self-healing workflows that replace manual operations.
* Build APIs and data platforms, that give DynamoDB teams and tools accurate, real-time views of capacity and usage.
* Reduce throttling, speed up limit increases, and make large-scale fleet events safe and predictable.
* Own features end to end, from design through deployment and operation, and deliver ambiguous projects with minimal guidance.
* Take part in on-call, debug issues across services, and fix root causes so problems don't come back.

**Description**
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.
  
  
Amazon WorkSpaces has protected and empowered enterprise work for over a decade and we are now reimagining what a workspace is. We are building Agentic WorkSpaces: a platform where the workspace itself is an active partner in how you work not just infrastructure that delivers applications. Today more than a million users rely on WorkSpaces daily; tomorrow those workspaces will host AI agents alongside humans — agents that code, troubleshoot, analyze, and act on behalf of their users governed by the same identity and security policies as the people they serve. We compete with Microsoft Citrix and Omnissa and we intend to leapfrog them by building the workspace that was designed for the agentic era not retrofitted for it.
  
  
Agentic Workspaces' On-Instance Software (OIS) is the layer that makes this possible from the inside of every WorkSpace: the operating system, provisioning logic, on-instance agents, telemetry, and update mechanisms across Windows and Linux. Our vision is for that software to be invisible — operating systems that launch within weeks of upstream general availability, agents that update themselves safely without disrupting access, provisioning that is self-diagnosable, and fleet management that works through the same AWS tools customers already use, delivered from commercial regions to classified partitions with automation as the default so quality and breadth improve release over release.
  
  
Knowledge of Linux operating systems Linux package management and native Linux desktop application development is desired.
  
  
You want to solve challenging problems in operating systems identity AI and desktop platform engineering at a scale that impacts more than a million users daily.
  
  
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to design, build, and operate the services and agents that provision secure and maintain WorkSpaces for humans and increasingly for the AI agents that work beside them across every supported OS and identity provider. As a developer on our team you'll own code end-to-end from design to development and work closely with senior technical leaders within the team and across AWS.
  
  
You will own end-to-end delivery of features and systems within OIS - from design through deployment and operations - holding a high bar for availability latency and security.
  
  
You are customer-obsessed technically deep and energized by solving hard problems. You think big about what the workspace of the future looks like — a unified agent shipping to two platforms from one code base, an identity model that treats humans and agents as first-class citizens, and autonomous troubleshooting that resolves issues before users notice — and then you build the systems to get there.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* : Design and deliver features and systems within On-Instance Software contributing to the architecture strategy for how the on-instance layer evolves to host and govern AI agents alongside human users.
* Drive the agent unification work that lets Windows and Linux features ship from a single code base making feature parity the default rather than a follow-up. Partner with EC2, identity providers, self-service troubleshooting, and platform teams - earning trust by driving technical discussions that result in impactful architectural decisions.
* Design and implement on-instance identity security and governance for a world where humans and agents share the same desktop: identity integration across the major join models, a trust and authorization posture that treats agents as first-class principals, and compliance-ready images built in rather than bolted on.
* Own the operation of low-latency high-availability provisioning and agent services used by more than one million WorkSpaces users globally. Ensure your services meet stringent SLAs across multiple production regions AWS partitions and OS variants with self-service diagnostics and autonomous issue resolution before customers are impacted.
* Drive engineering excellence through instrumentation automated testing and pipeline-based deployment - eliminating manual toil and shipping features simultaneously across Windows and Linux. Think big about the agentic era and experiment boldly with AI-powered capabilities such as conversational setup natural-language troubleshooting and AI-assisted fleet management.
* Raise the bar on customer self-service so operating-system breadth safe automatic updates and reliable provisioning are delivered without imposing an operational tax on the customer or the agent workflows running on the desktop.
